note: trial-067 was 138x slower per example than the esm2_t12_35M_coarse_go_terms trials, far beyond the ~81x parameter-count ratio alone. Both smoke tests showed only ~9.5GB peak VRAM against the 22.5GB budget with gradient checkpointing on - more than 2x headroom unused, paid for in recompute overhead. Separately, restricting LoRA adapters to only the last 18 of 36 layers (half) means PyTorch's autograd skips building/traversing a backward graph for the earlier 18 layers entirely (verified directly: their output activations have requires_grad=False with no adapter or enable_input_require_grads() forcing gradient tracking) - forward still runs for every layer, but backward, typically the more expensive half, only runs for the last 18. Combined into one trial rather than tested in isolation, given cost - a 3B trial is expensive enough that testing each lever separately wasn't worth the extra spend given both are well-understood in direction (both should help), only magnitude is unknown. Same batch_size/data budget as trial-067 for a direct, if not perfectly attributable, epoch-time comparison. VRAM risk: removing checkpointing could increase activation memory substantially (checkpointing's whole purpose is trading compute for memory) - if this OOMs, the fallback is restoring checkpointing and/or lowering batch_size.
